done: Theming TokenTable binds ORI-CONT-002's theming.mdx via render(entry)+<Content components={{TokenTable}}/> (apps/docs/src/pages/docs/theming.astro:60), 20 paired rows derived at build time from global.css with static light/dark columns and live swatches, theme-toggle.ts flips both html.light and html.dark and refreshes current-value cells on connect/click/reconnect; token-map vitest + both FLOW-SHELL e2e flows are green (3 projects each) and evidence is re-bound to the tip, approved at 32cf1a8 and merged to main as 446c98b.
deviations: FLOW-SHELL-01 AC-4 round trip uses the docs sidebar/body links (Theming→Dark mode→Theming) plus a separate full-load navigateLocalhost to /components/message for the code-frame check, rather than literally clicking header Components→message card→history-back, because the below-fold message card is not clickable on the mobile viewport (tests/sprint-05-orient-search/theme-toggle-persisted-flash-free.spec.ts:271).
concerns: playwright.config.ts:38 sets reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI, so any local run silently reuses whatever already answers on :4321 and skips the harness port guard — the reviewer reproduced FLOW-02 failing 3/3 against an orphaned ORI-AST-007 preview, and concurrent sprint tasks share that port.
ORI-AST-007's run_flow step runs pkill -f astro, which can kill a peer task's owned preview mid-run; there is no per-task ownership protocol guarding the shared port.
findings: Astro MDX does support render-time component binding via <Content components={{Name}}/> — the Sätteri compile destructures props.components and throws _missingMdxReference when absent, so the ORI-CONT-002 handoff note claiming 'no render-time component-mapping parameter' was imprecise (apps/docs/src/pages/docs/theming.astro:60).

getComputedStyle(documentElement).getPropertyValue('--code-background') returns oklch(23.5% 0 0) — Chromium re-serializes the lightness as a percentage — so live values must read the sibling swatch's resolved backgroundColor (number form) instead (apps/docs/src/scripts/theme-toggle.ts:48-53).

In .astro frontmatter, import.meta.url resolves to the compiled dist chunk during prerender (ENOENT on source paths), so build-time file reads must use process.cwd() (the docs app root) as the catch-all does, not import.meta.url (apps/docs/src/components/TokenTable.astro:28).

scope_impact.found: Live token values read via getComputedStyle().getPropertyValue() are re-serialized to percentages (oklch(23.5% 0 0)), diverging from the sheet's number form that the static columns print.
scope_impact.change: Read live values from the swatch's resolved backgroundColor (number form) or assert equivalence, and read source/token files via process.cwd() rather than import.meta.url.

scope_impact.found: The manuscript's bare <TokenTable /> is bound at render time through <Content components={{TokenTable}}/>, so the authored MDX needs no import and the binding is Astro-native.
scope_impact.change: Verify the binding through the static /docs/theming route's rendered tr[data-token] rows and DOCS-ONLY labels rather than looking for an import in the manuscript.

scope_impact.found: The playwright webServer reuse (reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI) can silently run the flow against a foreign task's preview, bypassing the port guard and invalidating the observed frames.
scope_impact.change: Record and verify the owned preview listener (PID/cwd/dist hash) before observation and refuse a listener not owned by the candidate.

scope_impact.found: The same shared-port reuse hazard as FLOW-SHELL-01 was reproduced: the cold-boot flow failed 3/3 against an orphaned ORI-AST-007 preview serving a table-less dist.
scope_impact.change: Record and verify the owned preview listener before observing the cold-boot frames and re-run with a genuinely owned preview.

scope_impact.found: Sprint tasks run concurrently and share localhost:4321, and one sibling's run_flow step issues pkill -f astro that can kill a peer's preview mid-run.
scope_impact.change: Give each task an owned preview PID/cwd record and either serialize the port or scope the kill to the owning worktree.
